limited_overlap.description: 1015 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 73,560 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
205 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10072 of 12000 applicants answered (83.9%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.45 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=0.0003, causal_forest=0.0006.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -8.4; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -0.42. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 6107 (90% -731 to 12944).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 4219 (90% 3325 to 5113); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -4375, without months_unemployed = 4875, without education = 5078; full model = 5247.
Run time 453 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10072.
